table.name: reservations

router_id.name: router_id
router_id.description: Identifier of the Neutron logical router (would join to the routers table). No data present, so the join is unverified.

status.name: status
status.description: Operational status of the router-to-edge binding (e.g. ACTIVE/ERROR/BUILDING in Neutron conventions). No values exist to confirm the code set.

status_description.name: status_description
status_description.description: Human-readable explanation accompanying the status. No data present; inferred from name only.

table.name: vips
table.purpose: OpenStack Neutron LBaaS v1 'vips' table: defines a virtual IP (listener endpoint) for a load-balancer pool, specifying the address/port/protocol clients connect to and the pool that backs it. The single row is an HTTPS listener on port 443 named 'spind.layer'. The actual IP address is held on the referenced port row in the 'ports' table (port_id).

admin_state_up.name: admin_state_up
admin_state_up.description: Administrative state flag: 1 = enabled/up, 0 = disabled. Stored as TINYINT boolean.

connection_limit.name: connection_limit
connection_limit.description: Maximum number of concurrent connections allowed to this VIP; -1 means unlimited.

description.name: description
description.description: Free-text description of the VIP; nullable and empty in this data.

id.name: id
id.description: Primary key; UUID identifying the VIP.

name.name: name
name.description: Human-readable name of the VIP (here 'spind.layer', likely the DNS hostname served).

pool_id.name: pool_id
pool_id.description: Foreign key to the load-balancer pool (lbaas 'pools' table) that serves traffic sent to this VIP.

port_id.name: port_id
port_id.description: Foreign key to the Neutron 'ports' table; the port whose fixed IP is the VIP address.

protocol.name: protocol
protocol.description: Protocol the VIP listens on; values like HTTP, HTTPS, TCP. Here HTTPS.

protocol_port.name: protocol_port
protocol_port.description: TCP/UDP port number the VIP listens on (443 for HTTPS).

status.name: status
status.description: Provisioning/operational status of the VIP (Neutron convention: ACTIVE, PENDING_*, ERROR, DOWN).

status_description.name: status_description
status_description.description: Optional human-readable explanation of the status; nullable and empty here.

tenant_id.name: tenant_id
tenant_id.description: Owning project/tenant ID (OpenStack keystone project UUID, here without dashes); used for multi-tenancy isolation.

table.name: vpnservices
table.purpose: OpenStack Neutron VPNaaS (VPN-as-a-Service) table: one row per VPN service instance, which attaches a VPN (IPsec) endpoint to a router and subnet for a tenant. Table is empty (0 rows), so meanings are inferred from the Neutron schema and surrounding tables (ikepolicies, ipsecpolicies, ipsec_site_connections, routers, subnets).

admin_state_up.name: admin_state_up
admin_state_up.description: Administrative state of the VPN service: 1 = enabled/up, 0 = disabled/down. Declared TINYINT used as a boolean; no data to confirm values (table empty).

description.name: description
description.description: Free-text human-readable description of the VPN service. No data to confirm.

id.name: id
id.description: Primary key; UUID of the VPN service. Detected as primary key; no sample values to confirm UUID format.

name.name: name
name.description: Human-readable display name of the VPN service. No data to confirm.

router_id.name: router_id
router_id.description: Foreign key to routers.id; the logical router to which this VPN service is attached. No join was detected (table empty), but the Neutron schema and the routers table strongly support this.

status.name: status
status.description: Operational/provisioning status of the VPN service (Neutron convention: PENDING_CREATE, ACTIVE, PENDING_DELETE, ERROR, etc.). No values present to confirm the exact codes.

subnet_id.name: subnet_id
subnet_id.description: Foreign key to subnets.id; the local subnet whose traffic is protected by this VPN service. No join detected (table empty), but schema context supports this.

tenant_id.name: tenant_id
tenant_id.description: Owning tenant/project identifier (UUID); the tenant that owns this VPN service. No data to confirm.
